visual_format: carousel (4 slides): labelled drawing, what was taught, results, limits
visual_text: A pessary holds the pelvic organs up
Many women change it in clinic about every 6 months
A pessary is a device placed in the vagina to hold the pelvic organs up.
What women in the trial were taught
changed in clinic, usually every 6 months
No clear difference in quality of life; fewer self-reported complications at 18 months
Women who looked after their own pessary also cost the NHS less. About half answered again at 4 years: still no clear difference in quality of life.
Vaginal tissue concerns on examination (ulceration, granulation or other): about 18 in 100 who self-managed, about 27 in 100 in clinic care. No test reported.

Not in the trial: women who could not use their hands well enough, women whose memory or thinking problems meant they could not consent or self-manage, women who needed teaching in a language other than English
About 1 in 5 women taught to self-manage went back to clinic care. Clinic care remains a good choice.
alt_text: Schematic side view of the pelvis with labels: a ring pessary sits in the vagina below the womb, with bladder in front and bowel behind. A pessary holds the pelvic organs up. Many women change it in clinic about every 6 months.

Two columns. Self-management taught: a 30-minute session, a leaflet, a phone call after 2 weeks, a helpline number. Usual clinic care: changed in clinic, usually every 6 months, shown with a nurse seated at a desk.

Trial of 340 women, 21 NHS centres, 18 months. No clear difference in quality of life; fewer self-reported complications. Bar chart: vaginal tissue concerns on examination 27 of 152 self-managing (about 18 in 100) and 43 of 160 clinic care (about 27 in 100). Self-management also cost the NHS less.

Limits of the trial. Not included: women who could not use their hands well, women with memory or thinking problems who could not consent or self-manage, women needing teaching in another language. About 1 in 5 women taught to self-manage went back to clinic care. Clinic care remains a good choice.
